title: Infant formula, Similac Sensitive, powder, made with tap water

content.title: About
content.content: Similac Sensitive is a powdered infant formula designed for babies with a sensitive digestive system. The formula contains partially hydrolyzed protein, prebiotics, and a moderate amount of fat to aid absorption and reduce the risk of colic. It is prepared using regular tap water at the recommended temperature.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula is specifically developed for infants showing signs of sensitivity to regular milk proteins.
It includes partially hydrolyzed casein, which is easier to digest than intact protein.
Prebiotic fibers support the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.
Similac Sensitive is available in various package sizes, convenient for travel.
Manufacturers recommend using water at 40‑50 °C for optimal powder dissolution.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Partially hydrolyzed protein reduces the workload on the gastrointestinal tract and lowers the risk of allergic reactions.

items.title: Balanced nutrient profile
items.content: The formula provides essential vitamins and minerals such as iron, calcium, and vitamin D to support growth and development.

items.title: Gut microbiota support
items.content: Prebiotics promote the growth of beneficial bacteria, enhancing immunity and digestive health.

items.title: Easy preparation
items.content: The powder dissolves quickly in warm tap water, simplifying feeding.

items.title: Suitable for sensitive infants
items.content: The composition is tailored for babies with heightened sensitivity to standard milk proteins.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Despite hydrolysis, some infants may still react to milk protein. Discontinue use and consult a pediatrician if symptoms appear.

items.title: Water quality requirements
items.content: Water must be safe to drink and at the recommended temperature; contaminated water can cause infections.

items.title: Overheating the formula
items.content: Excessively hot water can destroy certain vitamins and cause burns to the baby.

items.title: Incorrect dilution
items.content: Insufficient powder may lead to nutrient deficiencies, while excess can result in excess calories.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Measure the recommended amount of powder (usually one level scoop) and add it to 40‑50 °C warm tap water. Stir thoroughly until fully dissolved. Adjust water volume according to the infant’s age and pediatrician’s guidance.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Keep the lid tightly closed after each use. Observe the expiration date on the package and do not use after that date.
